relations.subject: data:document
relations.evidence: Primary key lookups are performed using the key-value API, which simplifies use and increases performance (as applications may interact with the KV store directly, rather than a secondary index or query processor).

relations.subject: data:document
relations.evidence: Documents can also be accessed using secondary lookups via [SQL++ queries](n1ql-query.md) and [MapReduce Views](../howtos/view-queries-with-sdk.md).

relations.subject: sdk:kv-operations
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - inverse direction from the usual case: here the sub-document/full-document write is the default and N1QL UPDATE is offered as the alternative for criteria-based updates
relations.evidence: or [N1QL UPDATE](../../../server/current/n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/update.md) to update documents based on specific query criteria:

relations.subject: sdk:kv-operations
relations.evidence: If you wish to only modify certain parts of a document, you can use [sub-document](subdocument-operations.md) operations which operate on specific subsets of documents

relations.subject: data:document
relations.evidence: It is possible to store and retrieve non-JSON documents as well, using a [transcoder](nonjson.md).

relations.subject: sdk:atomic-counters
relations.evidence: You can also use [sub-document counter operations](subdocument-operations.md) to increment numeric values _within_ a document containing other content.

notable_absence.finding: The page names CAS values, durability, and expiration as document-storage options but never states any RBAC role/privilege gate on basic CRUD operations themselves (unlike, e.g., provisioning-cluster-resources.json's index-management sections in round 3, which named 'Query Manage Index' explicitly). Basic KV CRUD appears to be documented as ungated by any specific named role on this page.

cross_component_finding: Strong confirmation of the round's reuse hypothesis at the server-cross-product level, not just within the SDK: this page's own definition of 'document' independently matches the promoted data:document concept almost verbatim ('A document refers to an entry in the database... has an ID... has a value'), and its Primitive Key-Value Operations section is the conceptual explanation of the exact operation set (upsert/insert/replace/get/remove) that sdk:kv-operations already covers - the same is true for sdk:document-expiration and sdk:atomic-counters, both minted from round 3's howtos/kv-operations.json and reused here unchanged. This page introduces exactly one new distinction the howto layer never named: sdk:transcoder, first surfaced by this page's own 'using a transcoder' phrase and only given full content two pages later in this same batch (nonjson.md).
